Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

input.command: cd /tmp; curl -si -XPOST localhost:8080/token; echo; T=$(curl -s -XPOST localhost:8080/token | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])'); curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" 'localhost:8080/orders?page=1' | head -c 1500

content.text:
`result.json` is written in `/workspace`. The shipped, discounted total for 1 March to 31 May 2025 (UTC) is **9,329,707 cents**, across **407 distinct orders**.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

The region figures add up to the total. I skipped 20 repeated listings (`duplicates_skipped` is 20).

- **Coverage:** I fetched all 30 pages. They hold 1,500 listings, which is 1,480 distinct orders plus the 20 repeats. Where an order appeared twice, the two copies were identical.
- **Calculation:** I applied the rules as you gave them, with an exact status match, UTC conversion before the date check, and each order's discount rounded half up on its own.
- **Service behaviour:** The service rate-limited me repeatedly (HTTP 429, retry after 1 second) and expired tokens at least once (HTTP 401). The script waited and fetched a new token each time, then repeated the failed request, so no page or customer was skipped.
- **Data quality:** Nothing else looked odd. Every customer id resolved, and every timestamp carried an offset or `Z`.

My working script is in `/tmp/w`, outside the workspace.
